sources.title: OOTP 6.5 official screenshot gallery — schedule, box score and roster
sources.observed: Historical gallery captions describe a daily schedule with probable starters, links to completed box scores/game logs, and player names linking to profiles. This is documentation of workflow; no current-edition or hands-on usability claim.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: keep fixture identity continuous across preparation, reporting and inspection; make performance rows lead to the actual player.
sources.avoid: Do not copy legacy desktop density or imply that an external Power Pros game supplies a game log.
sources.evidenceType: Official historical screenshot-gallery captions; opened 2026-09-18; visual geometry not independently measured.

sources.title: OOTP 12 official manual — Commissioner Portal
sources.observed: The manual separates commissioner actions, reports and tools. Team export checks include current-date status. Its automator can stop for missing exports and produces an operation-status log.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: make readiness and blockers actionable, distinguish them from presence, and show server operation outcomes alongside recovery restrictions.
sources.avoid: Do not transfer FTP mechanics, automatic file exchange, or one-click advance guarantees into PAWA.
sources.evidenceType: Official historical manual workflow description; opened 2026-09-18; no runtime evaluation.

sources.title: MLB The Show 24 official manual — More Ways to Play
sources.observed: The manual treats Postseason as a bracket-oriented mode and Custom Leagues as configurable season competition with friends. It does not document PAWA-style external-result approvals.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: let tournament structure dominate postseason; reserve celebratory framing for a verified championship.
sources.avoid: Do not import MLB bracket rules, assume feature parity, or call pending companion reports official.
sources.evidenceType: Official edition-specific manual; opened 2026-09-18; workflow reference only.

sources.title: NBA 2K11 official PC manual — Main Menu, printed page 13
sources.observed: The publisher manual, distributed on Steam CDN, distinguishes roster-management tools, sharing created content, and saving/loading files. Its historical online features are not evidence of present service availability.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: explicitly separate reusable roster/class files, public previews and mutations of an active league.
sources.avoid: Do not imply 2K compatibility, current 2K service support, automatic console upload, or a new marketplace.
sources.evidenceType: Primary publisher PDF; page 13 text read on 2026-09-18; menu semantics, not a contemporary visual reference.

sources.title: Football Manager 26 — Reimagined User Interface
sources.observed: The developer describes overview-to-detail interaction, task/message filters, an action panel, upcoming fixtures and a two-week calendar. It explicitly discusses readable type, contrast and platform-specific adaptation.
sources.adaptation: PAWA inference: surface the decision and its context first, use compact drill-down deliberately, and retain meaningful screen-specific structures.
sources.avoid: Do not turn every PAWA screen into tiles or treat developer marketing as proof of usability.
sources.evidenceType: Official developer feature explanation; opened 2026-09-18; no hands-on or comparative usability test.

screens.composition: A horizontal week band above grouped home/away series; fixtures occupy most of the canvas. Selecting one expands its state-specific action inline, with a compact opponent strip.
screens.primaryDecision: Which fixture needs my next action?
keep: Explicit pending, disputed and accepted labels
Prepare / Report / Review / Result according to permission
remove: A large scoreboard that hides the next fixture
screens.interaction: Move week, filter team, then select a game; return preserves week and selection. Pending scores never receive a final-result treatment.
screens.compact: Use chronological day groups, not a compressed month grid; status text stays next to score.
screens.difference: Time and series grouping are the organizing structure; it must not resemble the commissioner blocker queue.
unapprovedDependencies: Explicit date/day grouping requires verified schedule fields; do not manufacture dates from week numbers.

screens.composition: Away and home occupy opposing halves; central matchup metrics align on shared rows. The selected starter and own batting order sit below their team, not in generic KPI cards.
screens.primaryDecision: What lineup or availability issue should I resolve before this game?
remove: Decorative stadium occupying the decision area
screens.interaction: Open a player from a matchup row or move to the existing lineup workflow. Companion mode explains that preparation does not send changes into Power Pros.
screens.compact: Render paired metric rows above one full-width lineup chapter; never squeeze two roster tables.
screens.difference: This is a pregame comparison surface, while report is an entry workspace and box-score is a completed record.
unapprovedDependencies: Any new matchup calculation, export packet or lineup-writing control needs separate approval and backend evidence.

screens.composition: Persistent matchup and report-state strip; a wide entry sheet with team/stat selectors; a collapsible source-image lane and adjacent field-level errors; final review is a distinct summary stage.
screens.primaryDecision: Is the played result accurate enough to submit for review?
keep: OCR uncertainty and server validation beside the affected field
remove: Notebook decoration that reduces entry width
screens.interaction: Keyboard entry follows baseball columns; error selection focuses its cell. Submit shows pending review only after server confirmation; stale revision preserves the local draft for reconciliation.
screens.compact: One team and stat group per view; source preview toggles without losing entry position; review stays reachable at top.
screens.difference: The scorebook is editable and evidence-linked; its layout must differ visibly from both a read-only result and an approval decision.
unapprovedDependencies: Durable cross-device draft saving and new OCR capabilities are not approved by this layout.

screens.composition: One compact unavailable notice beside the actual matchup identity; underneath, supported destinations only.
screens.primaryDecision: Where can I continue with this game?
keep: Return to schedule or accepted result
screens.interaction: Focus the supported return action; a missing/inaccessible game falls back to schedule without inventing identity.
screens.compact: Single panel with normal back control.
screens.difference: A short dead-end recovery surface; no dashboard, ceremony or simulated broadcast shell.
unapprovedDependencies: Playable pitch-by-pitch sessions remain a separate engineering gate.

screens.composition: Round columns dominate the canvas, with explicit stage titles and series state inside each node. A selected matchup opens detail below the bracket rather than replacing it with cards.
screens.primaryDecision: What is the next eligible matchup, and how does it affect the path?
remove: Generic schedule list as the only desktop tournament view
screens.interaction: Select a node to review game or series details; retain the visible parent and next round. No unsupported manual reseeding control.
screens.compact: Round selector with ordered matchups and explicit previous/next path labels.
screens.difference: Topology, not chronology or numeric tables, is the primary reading order.
unapprovedDependencies: Do not invent elimination formats, tie rules, bracket repair or qualification guarantees.

screens.composition: One verified champion identity and season headline, a restrained trophy composition, then a factual final-series strip and entry into the season record.
screens.primaryDecision: Celebrate this verified season or inspect its record?
screens.interaction: Skip ends presentation only; view record does not advance the league. Missing champion yields an unfinished-season state.
screens.compact: Single portrait composition with legible score strip and visible skip/back.
screens.difference: This is intentionally the emotional peak; administrative pages must not reuse its hero composition.
unapprovedDependencies: New trophies, team art, audio and ceremony animation require art/implementation approval.

screens.composition: An ordered queue of current blockers occupies the main area; phase/week and active operation anchor the header. Reports, records and settings are secondary destinations grouped by task.
screens.primaryDecision: What prevents the league from progressing safely?
remove: Equal-weight grid of every dangerous action
screens.interaction: Selecting a blocker opens its exact record; pending acceptance and absent reports have different actions. Advance remains governed by server preflight.
screens.compact: A task list first; selection becomes a full detail route/panel with back restoring queue position.
screens.difference: A work queue organized by obligation, unlike the team hub and the permanent audit ledger.
unapprovedDependencies: New priority scoring, presence telemetry or force-advance behavior is not implied.

screens.composition: League/team context fixed above a dense player grid; a selected row opens a focused category editor. Changes appear in a review band before the permitted save.
screens.primaryDecision: Which exact live player field am I correcting?
remove: Hero athlete card before the editable fields
screens.interaction: Search team/player, edit one category, then review changed values where existing APIs support it; rejected saves retain inputs.
screens.compact: Select player first, then a full-width category form; search state survives Back.
screens.difference: Live-league correction with narrow scope; reusable file authoring belongs in roster-library.
unapprovedDependencies: New bulk edits, undo guarantees and before/after persistence require dedicated validation.

screens.composition: Class identity and filters above a prospect table; selected recruit expands attribute groups, with commissioner-only fields in a clearly marked permission region.
screens.primaryDecision: Which class record needs an authorized correction?
remove: Public-looking gem/bust badges in the list
Portrait-first card browsing for repeated edits
screens.interaction: Filter then open a record; hidden traits stay out of public preview/share surfaces. Saving confirms the named recruit.
screens.compact: List to one category form, with commissioner-only notice attached to the relevant fields.
screens.difference: This editor prioritizes class visibility and privilege boundaries; roster correction prioritizes existing team membership.
unapprovedDependencies: No new reveal rules, hidden scouting exports or unsupported class-wide edits.

screens.composition: Named file workspace with a team tree on the left, roster grid center, selected field controls below; Save and Save as are file commands in the header.
screens.primaryDecision: Which reusable roster file am I creating or saving?
remove: Ambiguous Save that could overwrite an unknown destination
screens.interaction: Choose source, edit, then save to a named library destination. Leave prompts preserve the draft on Cancel.
screens.compact: Team picker to player grid to editor; file identity and dirty state remain visible.
screens.difference: File scope governs the whole workspace; no phase, readiness or accepted-result chrome.
unapprovedDependencies: New formats, binary Power Pros export and cloud conflict merging remain unapproved.

screens.composition: A broad roster table supports browsing; Compare pins two named players into aligned metric columns with their source files retained above each column.
screens.primaryDecision: Which player or source roster best fits my intended use?
remove: Radar art that hides actual metric values
screens.interaction: Select two records explicitly; metric groups switch together. Open player details without losing the comparison pair.
screens.compact: A shared metric label followed by A and B values on each row; no two shrinking profile pages.
screens.difference: Inspection and comparison rather than authoring; the viewer should not inherit the studio edit controls by default.
unapprovedDependencies: Cross-edition rating conversion and automatic roster recommendations are not approved.

screens.composition: Library shelf of named classes leads to one class manifest. Recruit attributes use a table/editor workspace; Save, Share and Load into league are visibly separate command paths.
screens.primaryDecision: Save this reusable class or deliberately load it into a named league?
remove: One generic Publish command for three different outcomes
screens.interaction: Edit within the file; each outbound action states its actual destination and current visibility. Canceling Load returns to the unchanged draft.
screens.compact: Class list then recruit editor; Load opens its own destination review, not a tiny nested modal.
screens.difference: Class authoring is about reusable content and visibility; the live recruit editor is about a specific league correction.
unapprovedDependencies: New sharing permissions, marketplace metadata or non-destructive merge require approval.

screens.composition: A read-only manifest sits beside a concise source-to-destination transfer summary; outcome wording names library import versus league load as actually supported.
screens.primaryDecision: Do I want this shared file in the stated destination?
remove: Editable controls implying the source can be changed
screens.interaction: Preview recruits, then perform the supported import; success names what was created. Unauthorized destinations never appear available.
screens.compact: Transfer summary above a collapsible manifest; review and commit remain distinct.
screens.difference: A directional transfer review, not another library or recruitment page.
unapprovedDependencies: Duplicate detection, provenance signing and compatibility conversions need separate implementation.

screens.composition: A compact class cover introduces a browsable prospect contact sheet; selected profile is read-only and a clear import link ends the visit.
screens.primaryDecision: Is this shared class worth exploring or importing?
screens.interaction: Browse profiles without mutation; open the supported import workflow as an explicit next step.
screens.compact: List with optional small portraits; profile opens full width and returns to the same place.
screens.difference: Public discovery rather than file editing: imagery can lead, but no live-league controls or hidden traits.
unapprovedDependencies: New ratings, download counters, public author identity and sharing modes require approval.

screens.composition: A pending/disputed banner above submitted score and evidence; reviewed revision and submitter remain beside a compact confirm/dispute decision area. Team stat chapters occupy the main sheet.
screens.primaryDecision: Can I accept this exact report revision?
remove: A single optimistic green check for OCR, validity and approval
screens.interaction: Inspect evidence, choose confirm or provide dispute reason, then wait for server result. A changed revision requires deliberate rereview rather than silently accepting refreshed data.
screens.compact: Summary first, one stat chapter next, decision area reachable without losing review position.
screens.difference: This is a decision about another submission, not entry and not a final box score.
unapprovedDependencies: New automatic arbitration or evidence authentication is not implied.

screens.composition: Final-state scoreboard over a full-width line score; paired team batting/pitching tables underneath; recap is a secondary chapter with provenance.
screens.primaryDecision: What happened, and which supported performance explains it?
remove: Invented pitch sequences for reported games
Zeros substituted to complete an empty table
screens.interaction: Read result, switch team/stat group, then open a player or available recap; return restores the fixture.
screens.compact: Selected team table with curated column groups; unavailable data gets a concise explicit state.
screens.difference: A permanent read-only record; no evidence-upload controls or approval buttons.
unapprovedDependencies: New derived advanced metrics and factual recap claims require suitable supplied data.

screens.composition: Rows are teams/coaches; columns distinguish readiness, required report state and relevant blocker. The current advance operation sits directly above the matrix.
screens.primaryDecision: Whose unresolved obligation needs attention?
remove: Profile cards that hide missing obligations
screens.interaction: Open the exact missing report or permitted team detail from a row; no automatic message send.
screens.compact: Team rows become labeled status stacks; selecting one reveals obligations.
screens.difference: A cross-team readiness matrix inside the office, not a generic task-card collection.
unapprovedDependencies: Presence tracking and new reminders require explicit scope.

screens.composition: A short list groups routine progression, correction and recovery. The chosen action replaces the list with preflight evidence, affected scope and a single execution control.
screens.primaryDecision: Is this specific operation currently permitted and understood?
remove: All mutations visible as equally inviting buttons
screens.interaction: Review one action, execute once, then inspect its actual operation state. Failed/blocked actions explain the server reason.
screens.compact: List to a full-screen operation review; back preserves selection without executing.
screens.difference: Procedural action review, unlike settings forms and historical audit browsing.
unapprovedDependencies: New force, rollback or exactly-once retry guarantees remain unapproved.

screens.composition: Category navigation leads to a single settings form; current saved values and draft changes are visually separated, with phase-locked fields explained in place.
screens.primaryDecision: Which supported league setting should change?
remove: Settings mixed with immediate destructive actions
Sliders for unsupported or immutable rules
screens.interaction: Edit category, review valid differences, save; failed validation retains the draft and identifies the field.
screens.compact: Category picker and one form, without a long accordion of everything.
screens.difference: Persistent configuration rather than executing a one-time operation.
unapprovedDependencies: New rules, effective-date scheduling and role-transfer behavior require approval.

screens.composition: Dense time-ordered rows with actor, operation and target; selecting a row opens a read-only evidence drawer. Filters reduce the ledger without changing its ordering.
screens.primaryDecision: Who changed this record, and what evidence is available?
screens.interaction: Filter by available fields, inspect record, copy nonsecret identifier. UI never turns absence of evidence into a success claim.
screens.compact: Rows show time/action first; event detail opens full width.
screens.difference: Forensic reading and traceability; unlike a current blocker queue it includes completed history.
unapprovedDependencies: New diff reconstruction, export formats or audit retention promises are unapproved.

screens.composition: Compact invitation register with validity and permitted usage fields; selection exposes Copy or Revoke separately, with seat/coach assignment in its own area.
screens.primaryDecision: Which invitation should remain usable?
remove: Revoke adjacent to ordinary row selection
screens.interaction: Create or copy only through explicit actions; revoke names the selected invitation. No tokens in unrelated visual exports.
screens.compact: Named invitation list then actions; the token is deliberately revealed only where needed.
screens.difference: An access-management register, not marketing invitations or readiness tracking.
unapprovedDependencies: New invite expiry, seat limits or roles need backend support and approval.

screens.composition: Pending/disputed queue on the left; selected report evidence occupies the main area; decision controls bind to its displayed version. Accepted history is a separate filter/view.
screens.primaryDecision: Which report exception should I resolve now?
remove: Accepted and disputed scores styled identically
Bulk acceptance without full authorized review
screens.interaction: Select exception, inspect source and changed fields when available, then take the existing permitted action. Stale data blocks decision.
screens.compact: Queue to full decision sheet; return keeps filters and position.
screens.difference: League-wide triage leading into one report decision, distinct from a participant reviewing a single game.
unapprovedDependencies: New dispute rules, batch decisions and automated conflict resolution require approval.

screens.composition: Team rows align budget, recorded spending/obligations and available amount; selected team opens the existing allocation details and separately gated adjustment form.
screens.primaryDecision: What money is actually available, and does a correction need to be made?
remove: Invented transaction history from current totals
screens.interaction: Select team to inspect known accounting values; an edit names its precise field and scope, with server rejection preserved.
screens.compact: Labeled financial rows per team, then detail; keep numbers aligned.
screens.difference: An accounting inspection surface rather than a leaderboard or general editor.
unapprovedDependencies: Ledger reconstruction, currency conversion and new NIL policies remain unapproved.

screens.composition: Week/team matrix provides coverage context; a ranked diagnostic list below links to exact affected fixtures. Warnings and blocking findings have separate text labels.
screens.primaryDecision: Which proven schedule problem must be inspected before advance?
screens.interaction: Choose a check to highlight affected rows/fixtures; repair appears only if already permitted.
screens.compact: Diagnostic list first; chosen check shows its team/week slice rather than the entire matrix.
screens.difference: A structural inspection view, while the schedule is a coach’s chronology of games.
unapprovedDependencies: New diagnostics, automatic repairs and calendar assumptions require specification.

screens.composition: Entity-type selector above a searchable record list; one selected entity fills a categorized editor. Existing change history is adjacent but read-only until an authorized reversal is explicitly chosen.
screens.primaryDecision: Which named league entity and field should be corrected?
remove: Reversal portrayed as a harmless navigation action
screens.interaction: Select entity, edit category, review exact target and save. Preserve failed input and avoid implying bulk scope.
screens.compact: Record list to full form; breadcrumb retains entity and category.
screens.difference: Structural administration across entity types; dedicated roster/class editors optimize repeated player work.
unapprovedDependencies: Unsupported bulk mutation, reversible-history guarantees and new appearance controls need approval.

screens.composition: Timestamped snapshot rows align season/phase/week and known scope; selection opens a comparison of documented coverage and actual restore restrictions, followed by guarded action.
screens.primaryDecision: Is this recovery point compatible and actually restorable?
remove: Green Restore button where restoration is blocked
screens.interaction: Inspect scope first; disabled restoration explains the real restriction. A request in flight is not a restored league.
screens.compact: Snapshot list to a full consequence review; avoid nested confirm dialogs.
screens.difference: Recovery evidence and compatibility, not a file marketplace or ordinary Save as.
unapprovedDependencies: Complete restore, consistent snapshot coverage and revision-safe recovery remain engineering gates; no new promise.

screens.composition: Compact operation header with phase/week, server status and last known checkpoint; expand into a chronological status log only when useful or interrupted.
screens.primaryDecision: Is advance complete, still running, or in need of authorized recovery?
remove: Celebration before all required work finishes
screens.interaction: Allow safe navigation; return can inspect current operation. Recovery links carry the existing operation identity and do not imply safe automatic retry.
screens.compact: Status strip expands to one readable log panel.
screens.difference: A live process explanation, not a loading movie or a permanent audit ledger.
unapprovedDependencies: New cancellation, resumption guarantees and lease telemetry require verified endpoints.

screens.composition: A small operation-specific sheet names source, destination and visibility; only fields needed for Save, Save as, Share or replacement appear.
screens.primaryDecision: What will this file action change, and where?
remove: Nested dialogs over an already narrow editor
screens.interaction: Each action has a precise verb; cancel returns to unchanged draft. Server outcome updates saved state only after success.
screens.compact: Full readable sheet with persistent filename/context; no nested scrolling.
screens.difference: Small bounded file operation, unlike full import review or authoring workspaces.
unapprovedDependencies: New overwrite detection, recovery storage and share permission modes are unapproved.
